text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell sharply over the past week—dropping nearly 11% from $414.65 to $367.19—and today it continued that slide, losing another 0.2%. The decline coincides with crude oil prices falling from around $100+ per barrel two weeks ago to $89.53 today, a move that directly pressures refiners' profit margins. While US refineries are running at a healthy 95.7% capacity, the lower crude prices reduce the spread between what refiners pay for oil and what they can sell refined products for, which is core to their earnings.

Broader energy market shifts are adding headwinds. The emerging focus on renewable energy infrastructure (data center power, grid optimization, hydrogen catalysts) and new permitting rules could signal longer-term pressure on traditional refining demand, even as the geopolitical flare-ups in the Middle East haven't yet spiked oil prices higher to offset those concerns.
